title: [Chapitre] VIII. Analysis situs (quatrième mouture) : notes manuscrites (26/06-04/07/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 62-64 of the 4th version of 'Analysis situs', 1986). Grothendieck works with abstract 'magmas' M of loci (lieux). These carry combinatorial relations: an order X ≤ Y, a strict or 'interior' inclusion X <̇ Y, and an incidence or disjointness relation X ∘ Y, written |∘| or |·| in its 'external' form.

A 'fonction support' assigns to each X a closed subset |X| of a set or space P, i.e. an element of F(P). On the previous page:
- it is 'normalisée' if the |X| cover P and separate its points;
- it is 'fidèle' if conditions (ii) and (iii) hold together with X ∘ Y ⇔ |X|° ∩ |Y|° = ∅.
So the abstract disjointness relation is realised exactly as disjointness of interiors of the supports. This is a 'set-theoretic realisation' of the geometric configuration.

This page:
- The previous page observed that faithful support functions exist in every example he has touched (set-theoretic, topological, tame/'modérée' topology). He concludes that the existence of such a support function could be posed as an axiom 'sans inconvénient pratique'.
- The only exception is geometries of loci defined through a distance function. There the 'disposition' (separation) is described by distance > ε (or ≥ ε), and it cannot be reduced to a question of 'disposition ensembliste'.
- He adds that he has not looked at these metric cases closely enough to know whether the geometric language of magmas he proposes applies to them.

Example 1. Suppose that in a magma M the external disjointness relation is definable from the order: X |∘| Y iff there is no Z with Z ≤ X and Z ≤ Y (spelled out on p. 64). Then the map X ↦ Ouv(X), i.e. M → F(M), is a faithful support function. Here F(M) means closed sets of M for the Alexandrov-type topology attached to ≤, and |X| = M_{≤X} is the closure of X (p. 64). He exclaims that this already gives a large supply of examples. A margin note says it is a support function in the sense of pp. 30 and 71 and is normalised.

Page 64 then specialises to trivial or discrete magmas, where |X|° = {X}.

In modern terms, this is a representation theorem for an abstract 'region' calculus (part-of plus disjointness) by closed sets with disjoint interiors. The canonical model is the down-set (Alexandrov) topology when disjointness means 'no common lower bound'.
errors: No outright error. The claim that faithful support functions exist in all set-theoretic and topological examples is asserted without proof. The previous page's margin even says 'C'est inexact pour ... topologiques', so the axiom proposal is tentative.

In Example 1, faithfulness needs (ii) and (iii) to hold for the down-set closure, but these conditions are not recalled here, so the check is incomplete on this page. The disjointness part is clear. If disjointness means 'no common lower bound', then the interiors of the closures M_{≤X} and M_{≤Y} meet iff some Z ≤ X, Y, provided interiors behave as in the p.64 example where |X|° = {X}. In general Alexandrov posets the interior of M_{≤X} must be computed with care.

ideas.what: Abstract magma of loci with order and disjointness relations, realised by a 'support function' into closed sets of a space, faithful iff disjointness corresponds to disjoint interiors
ideas.modern_name: Representation theorems for mereotopological / contact algebras (regions as regular closed sets)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Whitehead, de Laguna (point-free geometry); Tarski; de Vries (1962); Düntsch–Winter, Dimov–Vakarelov (2000s representation of contact algebras)
ideas.where_published: Only in the unpublished Analysis situs manuscripts (cote 156); Esquisse d'un programme mentions tame topology but not this formalism

ideas.what: Proposal to take the existence of a faithful support function as an axiom of the theory
ideas.modern_name: Representability axiom (every abstract configuration has a concrete set-theoretic model)

ideas.what: Metric geometries with 'distance > ε' separation as the exception, not reducible to set-theoretic disposition
ideas.modern_name: Non-transitive tolerance/ε-proximity relations vs proximity spaces; tolerance spaces (Zeeman)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Efremovich (proximity spaces), Zeeman (tolerance spaces, 1962), Poincaré's physical continuum

ideas.what: Example: if disjointness = no common lower bound, then X ↦ closure of X in the Alexandrov topology of (M, ≤) is a faithful normalised support
ideas.modern_name: Down-set (Alexandrov) representation of a poset; canonical model of a 'disjointness from order' structure

missed.claim: Grothendieck's 1986 'magmas de lieux' with faithful support functions are essentially a region-based (point-free) geometry with a representation theorem by closed sets with disjoint interiors. This is the same problem later studied as representation of contact algebras / RCC-type mereotopology. He also isolates the metric 'distance > ε' case as the obstruction, which matches the known difference between tolerance relations and genuine proximity/contact relations.
missed.quote: La seule exception à cette règle concerne les géométries de lieux définis en termes d'une fonction distance, où la disposition est décrite en termes d'une distance > ε (ou ≥ ε)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It links Grothendieck's tame-topology foundations programme to mereotopology, contact algebras and qualitative spatial reasoning, a link apparently not made in the literature. It suggests that his 'Analysis situs' formalism could be compared with, or fed from, the Düntsch–Vakarelov representation theory.

missed.claim: Open question left by Grothendieck: does the magma language apply to metric ε-geometries, where separation is not set-theoretic?
missed.quote: je n'ai pas regardé ces cas d'assez près pour être sûr que le langage géométrique des magmas que je propose ici, s'y applique également
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This connects to coarse geometry, persistent homology (Vietoris–Rips at scale ε) and tolerance spaces, where scale-dependent non-transitive relations are central.

deep.surprise_reason: This is an unpublished foundational formalism of point-free geometry with a representability axiom. It anticipates mereotopological representation theorems and explicitly flags the ε-metric case. The content on this page is brief and partly routine (Alexandrov down-set example).
transcription_corrections: Line 2: 'surjectif [?]' should read 'support' ('l'existence d'une telle fonction support').
Line 3: 'dans un contexte [?] pratique' should read 'sans inconvénient pratique'.
'où la disposition est discrète' likely 'décrite' ('décrite en termes d'une distance > ε').
'et on peut dans chacun ramener à une question d'...' likely 'et on [ne] peut pas la ramener à une question de "disposition ensembliste"'.
'le cas [?] géométrique des imaginaires [?]' likely 'le langage géométrique des magmas', with 'applique' singular.
Example 1: 'dans les μ-espaces M, les |σ| sont définissables par ε̇' likely 'dans le magma M, la relation |∘| est définissable par ≤ (or <̇)'.
'est une fonction surjective {+fidèle+}' likely 'est une fonction support fidèle'.
'Ça en fait un bon foncteur!' likely 'Ça en fait un bon paquet!'.
Margin likely: 'NB C'est une fonction support (p. 30, 71) [...] normal[isée]', not 'foncteur surjectif'.
